rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In a report in the two Ṣaḥīḥs, he distinguishes gratitude to God for rain from attributing it to a star; the latter is disbelief in God and belief in stars, when meant literally.
rows.anchor: في الصحيحين عن زيد بن خالد الجهني أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أثر سماء

rows.speaker: اللغويون
rows.claim: Lexicographers commonly reserve qamar for the moon after conjunction and separation, from roughly the third through the twenty-sixth night; at other times they call it hilāl.
rows.anchor: والمشهور عند اللغويين أنه بعد الإجتماع مع الشمس ومفارقته إياها لا يسمى قمرا إلا من ثلاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers the common sense of qamar, the familiar celestial body throughout the month, especially because it is mentioned alongside the sun.
rows.anchor: ولعل الأظهر في الآية حمله على المعنى الأول وهو الشائع إذا ذكر مع الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God assigned the familiar moon specific stations and distances through which it travels, descending station by station.
rows.anchor: أي قدرنا هذا الجرم المعروف منازل ومسافات مخصوصة فسار فيها ونزلها منزلة منزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon reaches the later part of its course, when it appears close to the sun.
rows.anchor: أي صار في أواخر سيره وقربه من الشمس في رأى العين

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda identify the ʿurjūn as the palm-cluster stalk extending from the frond to its base; al-Ālūsī says this is the well-known explanation.
rows.anchor: وروي ذلك عن الحسن وقتادة وعن ابن عباس أنه أصل العذق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to explain ʿurjūn as the base of the date cluster.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنه أصل العذق وقيل الشمراخ

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another explanation takes ʿurjūn as the twig of the cluster that bears unripe dates; al-Ālūsī favors the first, more familiar explanation.
rows.anchor: وقيل الشمراخ وهو ما عليه البسر من عيدان العذق والكباسة والمشهور الأول

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj treats the nūn in ʿurjūn as extra, deriving its pattern as faʿlūn from the sense of bending and curvature.
rows.anchor: ونونه على ما حكي عن الزجاج زائدة فوزنه فعلون من الإنعراج وهو الإعوجاج والإنعطاف

rows.speaker: الراغب والسمين وصاحب القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib, al-Samīn, and the author of al-Qāmūs instead consider the nūn original, giving the pattern faʿlūl.
rows.anchor: وذهب قوم واختاره الراغب والسمين وصاحب القاموس إلى أنها أصلية فوزنه فعلول

rows.speaker: سليمان التيمي
rows.claim: Sulaymān al-Taymī reads ʿurjūn with ʿayn kasra, rāʾ sukūn, and jīm fatḥa, a dialectal form compared to bizyūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ سليمان التيمي ( كالعرجون ) بكسر العين وسكون الراء وفتح الجيم وهي لغة فيه كالبزيون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-qadīm here means old or ancient: the palm stalk has dried after time has passed; the resemblance is in its yellowing, thinness, and curvature.
rows.anchor: أي العتيق الذي مر عليه زمان يبس فيه ووجه الشبه الإصفرار والدقة والإعوجاج

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One reported usage sets a minimum of one year for qadīm, illustrated by a manumission condition freeing every slave of his that is qadīm.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أقل مدة القدم حول فلو قال رجل كل مملوك لي قديم فهو حر

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الرضا
rows.claim: A further report, transmitted by some Imāmīs from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā, gives six months as the minimum period of qadīm.
rows.anchor: وحكاه بعض الإمامية عن أبي الحسن الرضا رضي الله تعالى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not teach the Prophet poetry through the Qurʾān, whose eloquent teaching clarifies and distinguishes matters of origin and return.
rows.anchor: بتعليم الكتاب المشتمل على هذا البيان والتخليص في أمر المبدأ والمعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān differs from poetry in sound because it has neither meter nor rhyme, and in meaning because poetry relies on imaginative evocation while the Qurʾān gives judgments, beliefs, and laws.
rows.anchor: أما لفظا فلعدم وزنه وتقفيته وأما معنى فلأن الشعر تخيلات مرغبة أو منفرة أو نحو ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial that God taught him poetry indirectly denies that the Qurʾān is poetry: what God taught is the Qurʾān, and what was taught was not poetry.
rows.anchor: والمراد من نفي تعليمه صلى الله عليه وسلم بتعليم الكتاب الشعر نفي أن يكون القرآن شعرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement also implies that the Prophet is no poet; al-Ālūsī rejects the claim that this is merely an oblique allusion.
rows.anchor: وفيه أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام ليس بشاعر إدماجا وليس هناك كناية تلويحية كما قيل

rows.speaker: القائلون من الكفار
rows.claim: The opponents called the Qurʾān poetry and the Prophet a poet to portray his revelation as fabrication and imaginative fancy; al-Ālūsī rejects this charge.
rows.anchor: وهذا رد لما كانوا يقولونه من أن القرآن شعر والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم شاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parenthetical phrase confirms that poetry is unfitting for the Prophet: meter can force altered meanings, while exaggeration and distortion in poetry invite falsehood.
rows.anchor: لأنه يدعو إلى تغيير المعنى لمراعاة اللفظ والوزن ولأن أحسنه المبالغة والمجازفة والإغراق في الوصف

rows.speaker: ابن الحاجب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib argues that it would be irrational for the Prophet to compose poetry, since people might suspect revelation came from his own poetic faculty; removal of doubt leaves only their obstinacy, so the judgment falls on disbelievers.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الحاجب : أي لا يستقيم عقلا أن يقول صلى الله عليه وسلم الشعر لأنه لو كان ممن يقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī objects that eloquent prose could prompt suspicion as much as poetry, yet the Prophet was not barred from eloquence; the miracle itself removes reasonable doubt, so Ibn al-Ḥājib's cause is insufficient.
rows.anchor: فلو كانت علة منعه عليه الصلاة والسلام من الشعر ما ذكر لزم أن يمنع من الكلام الفصيح البليغ

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya locates the reason in poetry's imaginative ornamentation and embellishment; al-Ālūsī says this is the sound explanation to rely on.
rows.anchor: واختار هذا ابن عطية وجعل العلة ما في قول الشعر من التخييل والتزويق للقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates poetry's low standing in this context and that the Prophet lacked a poetic disposition, honoring him and distancing him from anything that could impair prophetic dignity.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية عليه دلالة على غضاضة الشعر وهي ظاهرة في أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام لم يعط طبيعة شعرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not giving the Prophet poetic ability, while also preserving him from composing poetry, removes a capacity that might harm his exalted office, by analogy with infallibility and protection.
rows.anchor: وإنما لم يعط صلى الله عليه وسلم القدرة على الشعر مع حفظه عن إنشائه لأن ذلك سلب القدرة عليه

rows.speaker: بعض الناس
rows.claim: Some infer from al-Mawāhib al-ladunniyya that the Prophet could compose poetry but was forbidden to do so; al-Ālūsī rejects this account.
rows.anchor: ويفهم من كلام المواهب اللدنية أن من الناس من ذهب إلى أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان له قدرة على الشعر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some hold the denial applies to all prophets because the verse gives no apparent reason to restrict it to Muḥammad; another view allows it to be particular to him as added honor.
rows.anchor: وهل عدم الشعر خاص به عليه الصلاة والسلام أو عام لنوع الأنبياء قال بعضهم هو عام لهذه الآية

rows.speaker: قائلون
rows.claim: Those who make the denial specific to Muḥammad say other prophets could retain poetic ability while being protected from composing poetry; this account treats the distinction as extra honor for him.
rows.anchor: وقيل بحوز أن يكون خاصا والنكتة زيادة التكريم لما أن مقامه صلى الله عليه وسلم فوق مقام الأنبياء

rows.speaker: آدم عليه السلام
rows.claim: If the report that Adam composed verses when his son was killed is authentic, it supports the view that the denial of poetic ability was particular to Muḥammad.
rows.anchor: وإن صح خبر إنشاء آدم عليه السلام يوم قتل ولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's spontaneous, accidentally metrical words at Ḥunayn do not make him a poet, since poetry is deliberately composed metered and rhyming speech; such rhythms can occur in prose.
rows.anchor: فقد عرفوه بأنه الكلام المقفى الموزون على سبيل القصد وهذا مما اتفق له عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some do not classify rajaz as poetry at all; al-Khalīl defines its base form as six mustafʿilun feet and calls its performer a rājiz rather than a poet.
rows.anchor: ما كان على مستفعلن ست مرات شعرا ولذا يسمى قائله راجزا

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: One account from al-Khalīl excludes the half-form (mashṭūr) and shortened form (manhūk) of rajaz from poetry; another excludes the four-foot majzūʾ form too.
rows.anchor: وعن الخليل أن المشطور منه وهو ما حذف نصفه فبقي وزنه مستفعلن ثلاث مرات والمنهوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative claim that the pronoun in 'is not fitting for him' refers to the Qurʾān is unsound: the preceding denial already excludes poetry from the Prophet, and the pronoun naturally refers to him.
rows.anchor: فإنه يكفي في نفي الشعر عنه عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: At Ḥunayn the Prophet recited Ibn Rawāḥa's line about lying awake while the polytheists sleep; this is an instance of quoting metrical speech, not composing poetry.
rows.anchor: وإنشاده إياه كذلك مذكور في البحر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says that after a finger was hurt in battle the Prophet recited a line about the injured finger and service in God's path; Ibn Hishām attributes it to al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, while Ibn al-Jawzī prefers Ibn Rawāḥa.
rows.anchor: أو ابن رواحة على ما صححه ابن الجوزي

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In a report, the Prophet quoted Ṭarafa's line that the days will reveal what one does not know and bring news from one not sent to ask; Abū Bakr corrected his wording, and he disclaimed being a poet.
rows.anchor: ستبدي لك الأيام ما كنت جاهلا ويأتيك من لم تزود بالأخبار فقال أبو بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه ليس هكذا يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aḥmad and Ibn Abī Shayba transmit from ʿĀʾisha that when awaiting news, the Prophet would quote Ṭarafa's line ending 'news from one not sent to ask.'
rows.anchor: إذا استراث الخبر تمثل ببيت طرفة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Ibn Saʿd and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmit from al-Ḥasan that the Prophet quoted the line 'Islam and gray hair suffice to admonish a man'; Abū Bakr took it as proof he was not taught poetry.
rows.anchor: كفى بالإسلام والشيب للمرء ناهيا

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن أبي الزناد
rows.claim: Ibn Saʿīd transmits from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī al-Zinād that the Prophet corrected al-ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās's verse order; Abū Bakr said he was neither poet nor poetry-reciter.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن سعيد عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي الزناد أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال للعباس بن مرداس

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Asked who the greatest poet is, the Prophet reportedly cited the poet who says that whenever he comes at night, he finds perfume there even if he brought none.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه قيل له عليه الصلاة والسلام : من أشعر الناس فقال : الذي يقول : ألم ترياني كلما جئت طارقا

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqī transmits from ʿĀʾisha, through a chain with an unknown narrator, that the Prophet never assembled a full verse except the aphorism about what one hopes for; she says he avoided its final inflection lest it become a poem.
rows.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي في سننه بسند فيه مجهول عن عائشة قالت ما جمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيت شعر قط إلا بيتا واحدا

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aḥmad's Musnad reports from ʿĀʾisha that poetry was the Prophet's most disliked speech.
rows.anchor: ففي مسند أحمد بن حنبل عن عائشة قالت : كان أبغض الحديث إليه صلى الله عليه وسلم الشعر

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: In the two Ṣaḥīḥs and other collections, the Prophet says a person's stomach being full of pus is better than being full of poetry; al-Ālūsī reads this as censuring excessive poetry.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحيحين وغيرهما عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لأن يمتليء جوف أحدكم قيحا خير له

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl is also reported to say poetry was dearer to the Prophet than much speech; al-Ālūsī reconciles this with ʿĀʾisha's report by distinguishing kinds of poetry.
rows.anchor: وما روي عن الخليل أنه قال كان الشعر أحب إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من كثير من الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān is an admonition from God and guidance for both humans and jinn, as the phrase 'a reminder for all the worlds' also says.
rows.anchor: أي عظة من الله عز وجل وإرشاد للثقلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is a manifest heavenly book, plainly not human speech because its inimitability silences those who challenge it.
rows.anchor: أي كتاب سماوي ظاهر أنه ليس من كلام البشر لما فيه من الإعجاز الذي ألقم من تصدى للمعارضة الحجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject of 'to warn' may be either the Qurʾān or the Messenger; the second-person reading supports the Messenger as subject.
rows.anchor: أي القرآن أو الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام ويؤيده قراءة نافع وابن عامر

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read li-tundhira, addressing the Prophet directly, which supports taking him as the one who warns.
rows.anchor: ويؤيده قراءة نافع وابن عامر ( لتنذر ) بتاء الخطاب

rows.speaker: اليماني
rows.claim: Al-Yamānī reads the verb in the passive; Ibn Khālawayh attributes this reading to al-Jaḥdarī.
rows.anchor: وقرأ اليماني ( لينذر ) مبنيا للمفعول ونقلها ابن خالويه عن الجحدري

rows.speaker: أبو السمال واليماني
rows.claim: Abū al-Sammāl and al-Yamānī are also reported to read with fatḥa on yāʾ and dhāl, from nadhira bi-shayʾ, meaning to know or become aware of it.
rows.anchor: بفتح الياء والذال مضارع نذر بالشيء

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī and al-Bayhaqī in Shuʿab al-Īmān transmit from al-Ḍaḥḥāk that 'alive' means rational.
rows.anchor: كما أخرج ذلك ابن جرير والبيهقي في شعب الإيمان عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the rational reading, the verse uses an explicit metaphor by likening intellect to life.
rows.anchor: وفيه استعارة مصرحة بتشبيه العقل بالحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, 'alive' means a believer, by contrast with the disbelievers; this explicitly likens faith to life, or treats faith as the cause of eternal life.
rows.anchor: أو مؤمنا بقرينة مقابلته بالكافرين وفيه أيضا استعارة مصرحة لتشبيه الإيمان بالحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense in kāna reflects what is already certain in God's knowledge; alternatives take it as future tense or as a prospective event cast as past, which al-Ālūsī dismisses.
rows.anchor: والمضي في ( كان ) باعتبار ما في علمه عز وجل لتحققه وقيل كان بمعنى يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warning is singled out for the living because they are the ones who benefit from it.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص الإنذار به لأنه المنتفع بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The 'word' that becomes binding on the persistent disbelievers is the sentence of punishment.
rows.anchor: الموسومين بهذا الوسم المصرين على الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Contrasting the living with disbelievers suggests that those lacking life's effects, such as knowledge, are truly dead; the wording may also contain a hidden metaphor signaled by another metaphor.
rows.anchor: وفي إيرادهم بمقابلة من حيا إشعار بأنهم لخلوهم عن آثار الحياة وأحكامها كالمعرفة أموات في الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning clause returns to the sūra's opening purpose of warning a people whose fathers were not warned; the transition from resurrection to Qurʾān and warning is strikingly apt.
rows.anchor: وكأنه جيء بقوله سبحانه : ( لينذر ) الخ رجوعا إلى ما بديء به السورة من قوله عز وجل : ( لتنذر قوما ما أنذر آباؤهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker looked toward the people of Hell and saw his companion there.
rows.anchor: ( فاطلع ( أي على أهل النار ( فرآه ( أي فرأى قرينه ( في سواء الجحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawāʾ means the middle, since the distance from the center to the surrounding sides is equal; ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar uses the word for one's middle in an expression to Abū ʿUbayda.
rows.anchor: أي في وسطها ومنه قول عيسى بن عمر لأبي عبيدة كنت أكتب حتى ينقطع سوائي

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن عباس وابن محيصن وعمار بن أبي عمار وأبو سراج
rows.claim: In Ḥusayn al-Jaʿfī's transmission, Abū ʿAmr reads the preceding 'those looking' with ṭāʾ still and nūn fatḥa; Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Muḥayṣin, ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār, and Abū Sirāj read fa-uṭṭuliʿa as a passive past verb.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو في رواية حسين الجعفي ( مطلعون ) بإسكان الطاء وفتح النون ( فاطلع ) بضم الهمزة وسكون الطاء وكسر اللام فعلا ماضيا مبنيا للمفعول

rows.speaker: قارئون
rows.claim: Other readings make muṭṭaliʿūn emphatic, followed by a subjunctive present fa-aṭṭaliʿa; another pair uses the lighter form, with either past or subjunctive verb.
rows.anchor: مشددا أيضا مضارعا منصوبا على جواب الإستفهام

rows.speaker: أبو البرهسم وعمار ابن أبي عمار
rows.claim: Abū al-Barahsim and, in Khalaf's report, ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār read the first word lightly with kasra on nūn, followed by a passive past verb.
rows.anchor: بتخفيف الطاء وكسر النون ( فاطلع ) ماضيا مبنيا للمفعول

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abū Ḥātim and others reject the reading that combines plural nūn with a first-person yāʾ; they expect muṭṭaliʿī, as in the analogous Prophetic wording.
rows.anchor: بين نون الجمع وياء المتكلم والوجه مطلعي

rows.speaker: أبو الفتح
rows.claim: Abū al-Fatḥ explains the extra nūn by treating the active participle like a present-tense verb, as in the cited expression of 'doers of good and its performers.'
rows.anchor: على تنزيل اسم الفاعل منزلة المضارع

rows.speaker: أبو الفتح
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī cites two poetic examples for the extra nūn, including a speaker asking whether his people will abandon him; this supports analogy with the verb.
rows.anchor: ما أدري وظني كل ظن أمسلمني إلى قومي شراحي

rows.speaker: أبو الفتح
rows.claim: The explanation treats the nūn as an added nūn of protection by verbal analogy; al-Ālūsī calls this the best account despite its difficulties, and notes that the pattern is rare outside poetry.
rows.anchor: ألحقت مع الوصف حملا له على الفعل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One critic says Abū al-Fatḥ's explanation only works in poetry; an alternative treats the attached pronoun as replacing detached iyyāya, then drops yāʾ and keeps its kasra.
rows.anchor: وضعف بعضهم ما وجه به أبو الفتح وقال : إن ذلك لا يقع إلا في الشعر وخرجت أيضا على أنها من وضع المتصل

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects replacing a detached pronoun with an attached one here because the construction is not one of the contexts that permits it; he prefers Abū al-Fatḥ's account.
rows.anchor: ورد ذلك أبو حيان بأن ما ذكر ليس من محال المنفصل حتى يدعى أن المتصل وقع موقعه وادعى أولوية تخريج أبي الفتح

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Other proposed analyses call the nūn a tanwīn or the final hāʾ a pausal hāʾ; al-Ālūsī notes objections, including that the cited poem may be fabricated and that moving the hāʾ only trades one poetic necessity for another.
rows.anchor: والبيت قيل مصنوع لا يصح الاستشهاد به وقيل إن الهاء هاء السكت حركت للضرورة وهو فرار من ضرورة لأخرة

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: On participles such as ḍāribuka, Sībawayh treats the attached pronoun as genitive by annexation, explaining the deletion of tanwīn and the dual or plural nūn.
rows.anchor: ذهب سيبويه إلى أن الضمير فيه في محل جر بالإضافة ولذا حذف التنوين ونون التثنية والجمع

rows.speaker: الأخفش وهشام
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash and Hishām instead treat the pronoun as accusative and the deletion as easing; retained nūn forms are evidence, though explaining them as tanwīn is disputed.
rows.anchor: وذهب الأخفش وهشام إلى أن الضمير في محل نصب وحذفهما للتخفيف حتى وردتا ثابتين كما في الفاعلونه وأمسلمني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭalaʿa and the forms with doubled or light hamza mean the same, generally intransitively; aʾṭlaʿa can also be transitive in the sense of showing someone something.
rows.anchor: وطلع واطلع بالتشديد وأطلع بالتخفيف بمعنى واحد والكل لازم ويجيء الإطلاع متعديا يقال أطلعه على كذا فأطلع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Abū ʿAmr's reading, muṭṭaliʿūn means 'those who will show'; the interlocutors are the agents, and their agreement to look first becomes the means by which the speaker is shown the scene.
rows.anchor: بمعنى مطلعون بالتشديد ونائب فاعل أطلع ضمير القائل والفاعل هم المخاطبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is a courteous, emphatic request; the fa-clause explains omitted wording, with an understood sequence in which they look and then he looks too.
rows.anchor: عليه بمعنى الأمر تأدبا ومبالغة

rows.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
rows.claim: The author of al-Lawāmiḥ says ṭalaʿa and aṭlaʿa can mean to come or arrive; on the passive reading he suggests an omitted source or prepositional phrase, but Abū Ḥayyān objects that a passive subject cannot be omitted.
rows.anchor: وعن صاحب اللوامح أن طلع واطلع إطلاعا بمعنى أقبل وجاء والقائم مقام الفاعل على قراءة أطلع مبنيا للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abaqa originally means a slave's flight from his master; applied to Jonah leaving his people without his Lord's permission, it is either metaphor or a metonymy using the restricted case for flight generally, with metaphor more eloquent. The ship called mashḥūn was full.
rows.anchor: وأصله الهرب من السيد لكن لما كان هربه من قومه بغير إذن ربه كما هو الأنسب بحال الأنبياء

rows.speaker: بعض الكمل
rows.claim: One eminent scholar defines ibāq more narrowly as fleeing a master so completely that a pursuer cannot find the runaway; Jonah's flight is figurative in light of that nuance.
rows.anchor: بحيث لا يهتدي إليه طالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds that narrow explanation strained once lexicographers' nuance is admitted, since nothing prevents applying it to Jonah's flight; he sees no force in denying the nuance.
rows.anchor: وفيه بعد تسلم اعتبار هذا القيد على ما ذكره بعض أهل اللغة أنه لا مانع من اعتبار ذلك القيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah drew lots with the people aboard; this verse is evidence for those who hold that drawing lots is lawful.
rows.anchor: فقارع عليه السلام من في الفلك واستدل به من قال بمشروعية القرعة

rows.speaker: من قال بمشروعية القرعة
rows.claim: Jurists who cite the event take it as evidence that drawing lots is permitted.
rows.anchor: واستدل به من قال بمشروعية القرعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mudḥaḍīn means those defeated by the lot, literally people slipped from the station of victory.
rows.anchor: فصار من المغلوبين بالقرعة وأصله المزلق اسم مفعول عن مقام الظفر

rows.speaker: رُوي
rows.claim: A report says Jonah announced punishment in three days, left before permission, and his people repented as it neared; ashamed to return after it was averted, he boarded a ship that stopped, and three lots selected him to be cast overboard.
rows.anchor: يروى أنه وعد قومه العذاب وأخبرهم أنه يأتيهم إلى ثلاثة أيام فلما كان اليوم الثالث خرج يونس قبل أن يأذن الله تعالى له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whale swallowed Jonah, taking him as a morsel, from the word luqma, a mouthful.
rows.anchor: أي ابتلعه من اللقمة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Aḥmad and others transmit from Ibn Masʿūd that a ship carrying Jonah stopped while others sailed; he identified himself as the runaway servant, and after three lots fell on him, he jumped into the sea.
rows.anchor: وفي خبر أخرجه أحمد وغيره عن ابن مسشعود أنه أتى قوما في سفينة فحملوه وعرفوه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd's account explains the sea-lots: each person received an arrow, with the one whose arrow floated selected and the one whose sank cleared; Jonah's arrow floated.
rows.anchor: وكيفية اقتراعهم على ما في البحر عن ابن مسعود أنهم أخذوا لكل سهما على أن من طفا سهمه فهو

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda, in a report from Ibn Abī Ḥātim and others, says the whale was named Najm, raised its head about three cubits, pursued Jonah around the ship, and caught him before he reached the water when he jumped.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه لما وقف على شفير السفينة ليرمي بنفسه رأى حوتا واسمه على ما أخرج ابن أبي حاتم وجماعة عن قتادة نجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mulīm can mean entering a state of blame, doing something blameworthy, or blaming oneself; the forms respectively signal entering, becoming, or causation with an omitted object.
rows.anchor: أي داخل في الملامة على أن بناء أفعل للدخول في الشيء نحو أحرم إذا دخل الحرم أو آت بما يلام عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid gloss mulīm as a wrongdoer or sinner, conveying the overall sense.
rows.anchor: وما روي عن ابن عباس ومجاهد من تفسيره بالمسيء والمذنب فبيان لحاصل المعنى

rows.speaker: قارئون
rows.claim: A reading with fatḥa on the first letter makes mulīm a passive participle; although the expected form from the wāw-root is malūm, it is shaped on līma, as in mashīb and muddaʿī.
rows.anchor: وقريء ( مليم ) بفتح أوله اسم مفعول وقياسه ملوم لأنه واوي يقال لمته ألومه لوما
